_comment: Curated devotional library. Text is never written here: BCP prayers come from the pinned Wikisource pages, Sanskrit verses from pinned Sanskrit Wikisource pages, duas from the bundled Tanzil Qur'an. Only titles for Hindu/Islamic items, tags and the short 'traditionally recited' explanations are editorial — and every item starts as draft for a faith reviewer.

traditional.title: The Sign of the Cross

passage.start: IN the name of the Father

traditional.explanation: Begins and ends prayer, tracing the cross from forehead to heart and shoulder to shoulder.

traditional.title: The Our Father (Lord's Prayer)

passage.start: OUR FATHER, who art in heaven

traditional.explanation: The prayer Jesus taught his disciples (Matthew 6:9–13), in its traditional English form, prayed by Christians everywhere.

traditional.title: The Apostles' Creed
traditional.explanation: The ancient summary of the Christian faith, shared across Catholic, Protestant and Anglican churches, and the first prayer of the rosary.

traditional.title: The Hail Mary

passage.end: at the hour of our death. Amen.

traditional.explanation: The angel Gabriel's and Elizabeth's greetings to Mary (Luke 1:28, 42), with the Church's request for her prayers. Prayed ten times in each decade of the rosary.

traditional.title: Glory Be
traditional.explanation: The short doxology praising the Trinity, prayed at the end of each decade and of the psalms.

traditional.title: Hail, Holy Queen

passage.start: Hail, holy Queen, Mother of Mercy

traditional.explanation: The Salve Regina, an 11th-century hymn to Mary, prayed at the close of the rosary and at night.

traditional.title: Prayer at the End of the Rosary

passage.start: O God, whose only begotten Son
passage.end: through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

traditional.explanation: Asks that meditating on the mysteries of Christ's life, we may imitate what they contain.

hinduism.title: Gayatri Mantra
hinduism.explanation: Rigveda 3.62.10, addressed to Savitṛ, the divine light. Traditionally recited at dawn and at the junctures of the day, asking that our understanding be inspired; it is commonly chanted after the opening syllables oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ.

hinduism.title: Mahamrityunjaya Mantra
hinduism.explanation: Rigveda 7.59.12, to Tryambaka (Shiva). Traditionally recited for healing, protection and freedom from fear, often 108 times. It is a prayer, not a treatment — keep your doctor close.

hinduism.title: Santana Gopala Mantra
hinduism.explanation: A prayer to Krishna as the child Gopala, traditionally recited by those hoping for a child and during pregnancy for the child's well-being. It is devotion alongside medical care, never instead of it.

hinduism.title: Santana Gopala Stotram
hinduism.explanation: The full hymn to Krishna as Gopala, traditionally recited for the blessing of children and for an expecting mother and child.

hinduism.title: Hanuman Chalisa
hinduism.explanation: Forty verses by Goswami Tulsidas in praise of Hanuman. Traditionally recited for courage, protection and strength, often on Tuesdays and Saturdays.

hinduism.title: Vakratunda Mahakaya
hinduism.explanation: Prayed to Ganesha before beginning anything — a journey, an exam, a new job — asking that obstacles be removed.

hinduism.title: Shantakaram Bhujagashayanam
hinduism.explanation: The meditation verse on Vishnu resting on the serpent — peaceful, all-pervading, lotus-eyed — traditionally recited before the Vishnu Sahasranama and in the morning for calm.

hinduism.title: Hare Krishna Mahamantra
hinduism.explanation: The great mantra of the holy names, given in the Kali-Santarana Upanishad; chanted on a mala or sung in kirtan.

hinduism.title: Ramaya Ramabhadraya
hinduism.explanation: From the Rama Raksha Stotram: salutations to Rama, the auspicious, the moon of the Raghu line. Traditionally recited for protection and peace.

hinduism.title: Manojavam Marutatulyavegam
hinduism.explanation: Taking refuge in Hanuman — swift as the mind, fast as the wind, master of the senses. Traditionally recited for courage before a difficult task.

hinduism.title: Mahalakshmi Ashtakam
hinduism.explanation: Eight verses to Mahalakshmi, giver of prosperity and well-being; often recited on Fridays and at Diwali.

hinduism.title: Sarva Mangala Mangalye
hinduism.explanation: The salutation to the Goddess as Narayani, auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, refuge of all. Recited to Durga for protection and blessing, especially during Navaratri.

hinduism.title: Sankatanashana Ganesha Stotram
hinduism.explanation: Ganesha's twelve names, to remove troubles (saṅkaṭa). Its closing verses say it traditionally: knowledge to the student, wealth to the one who seeks it, children to those who wish for them. Often recited on Sankashti Chaturthi.

hinduism.title: Ganesha Gayatri
hinduism.explanation: The Gayatri of Ganesha, from the Ganapati Atharvashirsha — chanted for clear understanding before study and new work.

hinduism.title: Shiva Panchakshara Stotram

shloka.reference: Śiva Pañcākṣara Stotram (attributed to Ādi Śaṅkara)

hinduism.explanation: Five verses, one for each syllable of na-ma-śi-vā-ya. Traditionally recited on Mondays and in the Shravan month.

hinduism.title: Ya Devi — for strength
hinduism.explanation: Salutation to the Goddess who dwells in all beings as power (śakti). Recited for inner strength, especially during Navaratri.

hinduism.title: Ya Devi — for wisdom
hinduism.explanation: Salutation to the Goddess present in all as intelligence (buddhi) — recited before study and important decisions.

hinduism.title: Ya Devi — for peace
hinduism.explanation: Salutation to the Goddess present in all as peace (śānti).

hinduism.title: Ya Devi — for prosperity
hinduism.explanation: Salutation to the Goddess present in all as fortune (lakṣmī).

hinduism.title: Ya Devi — the Mother
hinduism.explanation: Salutation to the Goddess present in all as mother — prayed for one's family and children.

hinduism.title: Kanakadhara Stotram
hinduism.explanation: The 'stream of gold' hymn to Lakshmi, traditionally recited for prosperity and relief from financial hardship, often on Fridays.

hinduism.title: Saraswati Namastubhyam
hinduism.explanation: Said by students before beginning to study: 'Saraswati, I bow to you; I begin my learning — may I always succeed.'

hinduism.title: Ya Kundendu Tusharahara Dhavala
hinduism.explanation: The beloved dhyana verse to Saraswati, white as jasmine and snow, holding the veena — recited before study, exams and on Vasant Panchami.

hinduism.title: Aditya Hridayam
hinduism.explanation: The hymn to the Sun taught by sage Agastya to Rama before his final battle — recited for courage, energy and health, traditionally at sunrise and on Sundays.

hinduism.title: Krishnashtakam
hinduism.explanation: Eight verses ending 'I bow to Krishna, teacher of the world' — sung on Janmashtami and in daily puja.

hinduism.title: Achyutashtakam
hinduism.explanation: A song of Vishnu's names — Achyuta, Keshava, Narayana, Krishna, Rama — loved for evening bhajan.

hinduism.title: Navagraha — Surya (Sun)
hinduism.explanation: The verse to Surya (Sun) from the Navagraha Stotram. Traditionally recited on Sundays, and in Jyotish when this graha's period (dasha) is difficult. Devotion, not prediction — please don't make big decisions out of fear.

hinduism.title: Navagraha — Chandra (Moon)
hinduism.explanation: The verse to Chandra (Moon) from the Navagraha Stotram. Traditionally recited on Mondays, and in Jyotish when this graha's period (dasha) is difficult. Devotion, not prediction — please don't make big decisions out of fear.

hinduism.title: Navagraha — Mangala (Mars)
hinduism.explanation: The verse to Mangala (Mars) from the Navagraha Stotram. Traditionally recited on Tuesdays, and in Jyotish when this graha's period (dasha) is difficult. Devotion, not prediction — please don't make big decisions out of fear.

hinduism.title: Navagraha — Budha (Mercury)
hinduism.explanation: The verse to Budha (Mercury) from the Navagraha Stotram. Traditionally recited on Wednesdays, and in Jyotish when this graha's period (dasha) is difficult. Devotion, not prediction — please don't make big decisions out of fear.

hinduism.title: Navagraha — Guru (Jupiter)
hinduism.explanation: The verse to Guru (Jupiter) from the Navagraha Stotram. Traditionally recited on Thursdays, and in Jyotish when this graha's period (dasha) is difficult. Devotion, not prediction — please don't make big decisions out of fear.

hinduism.title: Navagraha — Shukra (Venus)
hinduism.explanation: The verse to Shukra (Venus) from the Navagraha Stotram. Traditionally recited on Fridays, and in Jyotish when this graha's period (dasha) is difficult. Devotion, not prediction — please don't make big decisions out of fear.

hinduism.title: Navagraha — Shani (Saturn)
hinduism.explanation: The verse to Shani (Saturn) from the Navagraha Stotram. Traditionally recited on Saturdays, and in Jyotish when this graha's period (dasha) is difficult. Devotion, not prediction — please don't make big decisions out of fear.

hinduism.title: Navagraha — Rahu
hinduism.explanation: The verse to Rahu from the Navagraha Stotram. Traditionally recited, and in Jyotish when this graha's period (dasha) is difficult. Devotion, not prediction — please don't make big decisions out of fear.

hinduism.title: Navagraha — Ketu
hinduism.explanation: The verse to Ketu from the Navagraha Stotram. Traditionally recited, and in Jyotish when this graha's period (dasha) is difficult. Devotion, not prediction — please don't make big decisions out of fear.

hinduism.title: Mayuradhirudham (Murugan Dhyana)
hinduism.explanation: A meditation on Murugan riding the peacock — 'I worship the child of Mahadeva, protector of the worlds.' Chanted daily, especially on Tuesdays and Shashti.

hinduism.title: Subrahmanya Bhujangam
hinduism.explanation: Adi Shankara's 33 verses to Murugan of Tiruchendur, by the sea. Traditionally recited for healing and relief from illness and suffering, and on Skanda Shashti. It is a prayer, not a treatment — keep your doctor close.

hinduism.title: Kartikeya Stotram (Prajna Vivardhana)
hinduism.explanation: Twenty-eight names of Skanda from the Rudrayamala. Traditionally recited at dawn by students for clear thinking, memory and eloquent speech.

hinduism.title: Saha Navavatu (Shanti Mantra)
hinduism.explanation: The Upanishads' peace invocation, chanted by teacher and student together before study: may we be protected together, nourished together, and never quarrel. Lovely for children before school.

hinduism.title: Venkatesa Suprabhatam (opening)
hinduism.explanation: The dawn hymn that wakes Lord Venkateswara at Tirumala every morning, opening with Vishvamitra's words to young Rama. Recited at sunrise to begin the day with the Lord.

islam.title: Keep our hearts steady
islam.explanation: A dua of those firm in knowledge: that Allah keep our hearts from straying after guidance, and grant mercy.

islam.title: The dua of Adam
islam.explanation: The words of repentance of Adam and Hawwa: acknowledging wrong and asking for forgiveness and mercy.

islam.title: The dua of Musa for ease
islam.explanation: Musa's prayer before a daunting task: for an open heart, an easy path and clear speech. Many recite it before exams, interviews and difficult conversations.

islam.title: Increase me in knowledge
islam.explanation: A short dua for knowledge, often said before study.

islam.title: The dua of Yunus
islam.translationFrom: There is no Allah save Thee
islam.explanation: The prayer of Yunus from the darkness: affirming Allah's oneness and admitting wrong. Traditionally recited in distress.

islam.title: The dua of Zakariya for a child
islam.explanation: Zakariya's prayer for righteous offspring. Many recite it when hoping for a child and during pregnancy — alongside medical care, never instead of it.

islam.title: Comfort of our eyes
islam.explanation: A dua for one's spouse and children to be a comfort, and to lead in goodness.

islam.title: Mercy for my parents
islam.explanation: The dua for one's parents, asking mercy for them as they cared for us when we were small.

islam.title: Forgive and have mercy
islam.explanation: A short dua for forgiveness and mercy.

islam.title: Allah is sufficient for me
islam.explanation: Words of trust in Allah, traditionally repeated in worry.

islam.title: Ayat al-Kursi
islam.explanation: The Verse of the Throne, on Allah's majesty and care. Traditionally recited for protection, after prayers and before sleep.

islam.title: Surah Al-Ikhlas
islam.explanation: The surah of sincere faith in Allah's oneness.

islam.title: Surah Al-Falaq
islam.explanation: Seeking refuge in the Lord of the daybreak. With Al-Ikhlas and An-Nas, traditionally recited morning and evening and before sleep.

islam.title: Surah An-Nas
islam.explanation: Seeking refuge in the Lord of mankind from whispered harm.
